name: Lancashire Combined County Authority (LCCA)
established: Formally launched 5 February 2025 (Lancashire Combined County Authority Regulations 2025; shadow authority first met 27 November 2024)
mayoralNote: Non-mayoral, led by a chair; government has said Lancashire will get a mayor within ~18 months, alongside reorganisation

functions.name: Local Transport Authority role
functions.detail: LCCA became the LTA for all three constituent councils on 1 April 2026, with a £640m transport funding settlement over four years

functions.name: Adult Skills Fund
functions.detail: £40.8m adult education/skills budget administered by the LCCA from August 2026 (previously central government)

functions.name: Proposed
functions.detail: Housing, wider education and skills, and environmental functions proposed under the devolution deal

infancyNote: The CCA is in its infancy: strategy and funding are lifting to CCA level, but delivery capacity still sits with LCC and the two existing unitaries. No published disaggregation shows what part of any council's net budget transfers to the CCA.
postLgrNote: After vesting day the CCA's constituent members will be drawn from the successor unitaries; Lancashire's end-state is four unitary councils plus one (likely mayoral) combined authority: five bodies, not four.
